Predictions as to Ammon, Idumea, Damascus, Kedar, Hazor, and Elam.</title> <div sID="gen18998" type="x-p"/> The event of the prophecy as to Ammon preceded that as to Moab (see on <reference osisRef="Jer.49.3">Jr 49:3</reference>); and in <reference osisRef="Ezek.21.26-Ezek.21.28">Eze 21:26-28</reference>, the destruction of Ammon is subjoined to the deposition of Zedekiah.<div eID="gen18998" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen18999" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10630"/><hi type="bold">1. Hath Israel ... no heir?--</hi>namely, to occupy the land of Gad, after it itself has been carried away captive by Shalmaneser. Ammon, like Moab, descended from Lot, lay north of Moab, from which it was separated by the river Arnon, and east of Reuben and Gad (<reference osisRef="Josh.13.24">Jos 13:24</reference>, <reference osisRef="Josh.13.25">25</reference>) on the same side of Jordan. It seized on Gad when Israel was carried captive. Judah was by the right of kindred the heir, not Ammon; but Ammon joined with Nebuchadnezzar against Judah and Jerusalem (<reference osisRef="2Kgs.24.2">2Ki 24:2</reference>) and exulted over its fall (<reference osisRef="Ps.83.4-Ps.7.8">Psa 83:4-7, 8</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zeph.2.8">Zep 2:8</reference>, <reference osisRef="2Cor.2.9">9</reference>). It had already, in the days of Jeroboam, in Israel's affliction, tried to "enlarge its border" (<reference osisRef="2Kgs.14.26">2Ki 14:26</reference>; <reference osisRef="Amos.1.1">Am 1:1</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Cor.1.13">13</reference>).<div eID="gen18999" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19000" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">their king--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Amos.1.15">Am 1:15</reference>); referring to Melchom, their tutelary idol (<reference osisRef="Zeph.1.5">Zep 1:5</reference>); and so the Septuagint reads it here as a proper name (<reference osisRef="1Kgs.11.5">1Ki 11:5</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Kgs.11.33">33</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Kgs.23.13">2Ki 23:13</reference>). The Ammonite god is said to do what they do, namely, occupy the Israelite land of Gad. To Jehovah, the theocratic "King" of Israel, the land belonged of right; so that their Molech or Melchom was a usurper-king.<div eID="gen19000" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19001" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">his people--</hi>the people of Melchom, "their king." Compare "people of Chemosh," <reference osisRef="Jer.48.46">Jr 48:46</reference>. <div eID="gen19001" type="x-p"/>

Compare "people of Chemosh," Jr 48:46 .

entries.content_plain: 5. every man right forth-- whithersoever chance may lead him ( Jr 46:5 ; Ge 19:17 ); straight before him, onwards at random ( Am 4:3 ). none ... gather up him, &c.-- There shall be none to gather together the wandering fugitives, so as to care for them and restore them to their own homes.

Obadiah's was fulfilled probably in Sennacherib's time (compare <reference osisRef="Isa.34.5">Is 34:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="Amos.1.11">Am 1:11</reference>); Jeremiah's about the same time as his preceding prophecies (<reference osisRef="Jer.49.12">Jr 49:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.25.12">Eze 25:12</reference>).<div eID="gen19015" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19016" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">wisdom--</hi>for which the Arabs and the people of Teman (a city of Edom) in particular, were famed (<reference osisRef="Gen.36.15">Ge 36:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Kgs.4.30">1Ki 4:30</reference>; see Job, everywhere; Ob 8).<div eID="gen19016" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19017" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">vanished--</hi>literally, "poured out," that is, exhausted (compare <reference osisRef="Isa.19.3">Is 19:3</reference>, Margin) [Maurer]. Or, as the kindred Ethiopic word means, "worn out" [Ludovicus De Dieu]. <div eID="gen19017" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 7. Concerning Edom-- a distinct prophecy, copied in part from Obadiah, but with the freedom of one himself inspired and foretelling a later calamity. Obadiah's was fulfilled probably in Sennacherib's time (compare Is 34:5 ; Am 1:11 ); Jeremiah's about the same time as his preceding prophecies ( Jr 49:12 ; Eze 25:12 ). wisdom-- for which the Arabs and the people of Teman (a city of Edom) in particular, were famed ( Ge 36:15 ; 1Ki 4:30 ; see Job, everywhere; Ob 8). vanished-- literally, "poured out," that is, exhausted (compare Is 19:3 , Margin) [Maurer]. Or, as the kindred Ethiopic word means, "worn out" [Ludovicus De Dieu].

Prophecy as to Damascus, &c. (<reference osisRef="Isa.17.1">Is 17:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.10.9">10:9</reference>). The kingdom of Damascus was destroyed by Assyria, but the city revived, and it is as to the latter Jeremiah now prophesies. The fulfilment was probably about five years after the destruction of Jerusalem by Nebuchadnezzar [Josephus, Antiquities, 10.9,7].<div eID="gen19057" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19058" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Hamath is confounded--</hi>at the tidings of the overthrow of the neighboring Damascus.<div eID="gen19058" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19059" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">on the sea--</hi>that is, at the sea; the dwellers there are alarmed. Other manuscripts read, "like the sea." "There is anxiety (restless) as is the sea: they cannot quiet it," that is, it cannot be quieted (<reference osisRef="Isa.57.20">Is 57:20</reference>).<div eID="gen19059" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19060" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">it--</hi>Whatever dwellers are there "cannot be quiet." <div eID="gen19060" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 23. Prophecy as to Damascus, &c. ( Is 17:1 ; 10:9 ). The kingdom of Damascus was destroyed by Assyria, but the city revived, and it is as to the latter Jeremiah now prophesies. entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10653"/><div sID="gen19061" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10653"/><hi type="bold">25. city of praise--</hi>The prophet, in the person of a citizen of Damascus deploring its calamity, calls it "the city of praise," that is, celebrated with praises everywhere for its beauty (<reference osisRef="Jer.33.9">Jr 33:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.51.41">51:41</reference>). "How is it possible that such a city has not been left whole--has not been spared by the foe?" Compare left, <reference osisRef="Luke.17.35">Lu 17:35</reference>, <reference osisRef="Luke.17.36">36</reference>. So Israel "left" standing some of the Canaanite cities (<reference osisRef="Josh.11.13">Jos 11:13</reference>).<div eID="gen19061" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19062" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">of my joy--</hi>that is, in which I delighted. <div eID="gen19062" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10666"/><div sID="gen19084" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10666"/>38. I will show Myself King by My judgments there, as though My tribunal were erected there. The throne of Cyrus, God's instrument, set up over Media, of which Elam was a part, may be meant [Grotius]; or rather, that of Nebuchadnezzar (<reference osisRef="Jer.43.10">Jr 43:10</reference>). Then the restoration of Elam (<reference osisRef="Jer.49.39">Jr 49:39</reference>) will refer partly to that which took place on the reduction of Babylon by Cyrus, prince of Persia and Media. <div eID="gen19084" type="x-p"/>
